answer: Proof of Replication resists Sybil attacks by forcing each agent to seal key-bound data through chained block cipher layers, post a Merkle root, and answer random slice audits under strict timeouts. Because recomputing unstored bytes requires serial steps, a CPU at its clock-speed summit cannot cheat in time, making attackers buy dedicated storage per identity instead of turning stateless clouds into a Sybil haven. However, slow sealing bars ephemeral agents from rapid onboarding.
